chapter: England, Paris and memories of Kansas City and Harlem
title: Disliking life abroad; English food and the S.S. United cooks
summary: She prefers America. Rationing was bad, so the S.S. United's crew brought her steaks; she slipped away rather than face a birthday party.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Just before you get to Paris, Mary - England was the first time you had ever been out of the country?
How did you like living some place other than the United States?
I really don't know what people like about foreign countries. I don't know, maybe I'm corny. I don't

like it; I like America. The English were very nice to me and all that and also Paris, but I just like Americans. I wouldn't want to live there. I like to go for a short visit. I stayed in England and the food during that time was very bad, you know, people still didn't have food. The guys on the S. S. United, they used to bring me 20 and 25 steaks and the cook would cook me something special. So one day I had a birthday there and they wanted to give a party for me on the ship. They were coming in. The newspaper people are the people that held me over, so they were holding me over for the third time. I decided I didn't want any more of England so I packed all my bags and closed them up and left the door open. They brought the cake in and steaks and everything but I had left. I went to Paris.
